batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 candidate IDs and their exact supplied premeasurement predictions. Combine targeted follow-up of endpoint-specific loading associations and boundary-shape failures with missing response segments in related esters, ketones, aldehydes and basic compounds. Use matched conditions where available, and avoid redundant catalog rows representing the same tuple.

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading associations are molecule- and ratio-dependent, can be nonlinear, and can move onset and completion differently. Recent midpoint labels support localized onset changes, while benzyl benzoate and terephthalaldehyde show substantial completion associations. These contrasts do not establish a universal loading mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many supplied forecasts barely change across loading. Targeted contrasts can teach when that insensitivity is appropriate and when V1 and V2 require different responses, without assigning every recorded difference to loading causally.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does benzyl-benzoate completion growth develop before 100/1, does it transfer to alkyl benzoates, and do the thioglycolate, dialdehyde and loading-solvent-volume comparisons preserve their endpoint-specific associations?

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response curvature and endpoint coupling depend on the local structural environment. The recent cyclic-ketone, propiophenone and aromatic-carbonyl results support learning response segments locally rather than applying a common carbonyl or ester offset.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related acceptor-containing molecules have different transition locations and different onset/completion relationships. Missing curve segments in sparsely measured environments can improve transfer across many rows while limiting corrections to their supported scope.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected o-methylacetophenone, m-tolualdehyde, fluorobenzoate, thioglycolate and lipophilic-acrylate points follow their predicted response shapes or expose structural overtransfer?

hypotheses.content: The nearly coincident high-loading records for m77 at 2/1 and m57 at 50/1 do not describe their entire loading series. Their extent across adjacent ratios remains unresolved, and the available comparisons cannot identify an unrecorded mechanism or establish measurement error.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest ordinary lower-loading labels show that transferring these exceptional outcomes broadly produces errors. Independent ratio points can delimit appropriate transfer without repeatedly measuring an already characterized tuple.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m77 ordinary at high-loading 10/1, and does m57 develop a late onset at 20/1 only at high loading, at both loadings, or at neither?

hypotheses.content: Strong-eluent extrema transfer unreliably between scaffolds and conditions. The predicted pure-EA maxima for m29 and m130 and the deep 1/1 fluorenone trough were not supported at the selected tuples. Other measured boundary reversals remain, so neither universal monotonicity nor universal reversal is justified.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Boundary predictions cover many remaining rows. Testing persistent or adjacent extrema can repair a recurring response-shape failure while preserving genuine scaffold-specific recorded behavior.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does fluorenone retain the predicted 2/1 trough, does m29's pure-EA correction extend to 150 uL, and are the pure-EA maxima predicted for methylacetophenone and the two propiophenones supported?

hypotheses.content: Basic nitrogen environments may have distinct early solvent-response and loading relationships. Existing amino-ester and tertiary-amine observations motivate testing where these differences emerge under stronger eluent; silica-interaction priors do not establish a shared amine correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Early labels can constrain structural transfer before steep retention growth and prevent later errors from inducing an offset across all conditions of basic compounds. Cross-isomer comparisons remain confounded by their recorded loading conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the para and ortho ethyl amino esters have the predicted 1/1 responses, and is the tertiary amino-acrylate onset loading contrast already present under pure EA?

feedback_interpretation:
The strongest new failure was benzyl benzoate at 100/1 and 150 uL: 36b45fbdbace5950c108 measured 32.72/61.66 mL, with acquisition-time errors of -5.43/-19.88 mL. Its completion is much later than the low-loading 100/1 observation, whereas onset differs considerably less. I therefore select the missing high-loading 50/1 segment and an alkyl-benzoate comparison to test the scope of this association.

The m186 and dibenzoylmethane midpoint labels changed the loading interpretation. At 50/1, 2efa93ea474f798b712a and 5ba8cead5a790ba93029 had onsets near 5 mL, matching their higher-loading references more closely than their low-loading references. This weakens smooth interpolation of onset across loading. Terephthalaldehyde's latest 5/1 label extended completion to 38.12 mL while onset stayed near the midpoint value. The ethyl p-methoxybenzoate series also showed earlier onset and later completion with increasing loading. These outcomes favor local, endpoint-specific experiments.

The boundary tests rejected two large predicted pure-EA completion maxima: m29 and m130 measured 7.99 and 6.97 mL completion, respectively. Fluorenone at 1/1 finished at 18.88 mL, substantially later than its historical 12.61 mL forecast, although still slightly earlier than its measured pure-EA completion. The current predictor retains a fluorenone trough at 2/1 and several other boundary maxima, which now receive direct tests.

Both lower-loading m77 measurements at 2/1 were ordinary, as was low-loading m57 at 50/1. This supports condition-local interpretations of their exceptional high-loading records and motivates adjacent-ratio tests. The m63 curve showed an increasing completion shortfall toward 50/1, while m64's measured 20/1 response was flatter than forecast. Meanwhile, the m40 low-loading 20/1 prediction was accurate. I retain scaffold-specific curvature as useful and move exploration to less-complete response environments. All errors discussed here are acquisition-time feedback, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The batch contains exactly 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs, with no duplicate molecule-condition tuples within the selection and no pending experiments. The exact predictions associated with these IDs in this packet are frozen before measurement; numerical forecasts in the reasons are abbreviated descriptions of those supplied values.

The loading experiments address specific unresolved relationships. Benzyl benzoate and isobutyl benzoate test the reach of the latest completion failure. The thioglycolate series combines a ratio segment with a matched loading contrast. Terephthalaldehyde and acetoxybenzaldehyde examine whether onset and completion associations begin early, while the dibenzoylmethane comparison isolates recorded loading-solvent volume at fixed sample loading. These experiments can teach interactions rather than merely reinforce molecule-level averages.

Boundary experiments follow concrete failed hypotheses and remaining predicted extrema. The m23 pair separately tests compressed early intervals in a short-retention region. The m57 pair and m77 point delimit transfer from exceptional records. Missing ketone, aldehyde, amino-ester and acrylate segments provide exploration where labels can clarify structure-condition relationships. Pentafluorobenzene supplies a useful comparison for completion growth with little onset movement outside polar families.

Across the full supplied pool, many rows repeat already measured tuples or offer closely related short-retention baselines. The selected gaps offer more distinct questions while retaining coverage of that common short-retention regime. Quantile widths were secondary evidence: they are single-predictor outputs, many completion q10 values are zero, and some quantiles cross. Elution interval width is used only as a measured or predicted chromatographic property. The expected benefit is better overall Row V1/V2 generalization through more accurate response shapes and more selective structural and loading transfer; unrecorded experimental factors remain a limit on causal interpretation.
